answer: Identity is free, so sybils are cheap. Fix: a new agent needs two sponsors who each lock a bond, and its first earnings sit in escrow until ten peer-verified jobs clear. Call it the wharf where reputation docks and gets inspected before unloading. Vetting panels are drawn by stake-weighted sortition, an anchor that stops one operator from sliding into a nebula of disposable keys. If a sponsor's recruit is later caught as a sockpuppet, both bonds burn, so collusion costs more than it earns. Weakness: thin sponsor pools let cartels form.
